import { addDays, weekdayOf } from './dates.js';

/** Tells whether a branch is open on a calendar date: not on a closed weekday and not on a holiday. */
export function isOpenOn(branch, isoDate) {
  return !branch.closedWeekdays.includes(weekdayOf(isoDate)) && !branch.holidays.includes(isoDate);
}

/** Returns the first date on or after `isoDate` on which the branch is open. */
export function nextOpenDay(branch, isoDate) {
  let day = isoDate;
  while (!isOpenOn(branch, day)) day = addDays(day, 1);
  return day;
}

content.text:
A branch's closures now count as closed days, so loan due dates and hold pickup deadlines can no longer fall inside one. All 66 tests pass, including the two I added.

The fix is in `isOpenOn` in `lib/helpers/opening-days.js`. A date inside any `{ from, to }` closure, both ends included, now counts as closed. A branch with no `closures` field behaves as before.

`computeDueDate` and `pickupDeadline` both already call `nextOpenDay`, which uses `isOpenOn`, so neither needed changes. Nothing else in `lib` checks opening days.

I added tests in `test/dates.test.js` and `test/due-dates.test.js`. They cover the first and last day of a closure, the days just outside it, and a loan whose due date lands in the closure and moves to the day the branch reopens. I didn't add a test for the hold pickup deadline. It uses the same helper, but `pickupDeadline` looks branches up from the config, which has no closures to test with. I also didn't add a closure to any real branch in `lib/config/branches.js`, since you didn't give me one.

My first version of the closure test used a Sunday as the day before the closure, so it failed. That was a mistake in the test, not in the code, and I fixed the test.
